definitions.explanation: Something that has just been made or prepared, implying it is at its freshest or best state. Used especially for food, but also for other crafted items.

examples.japanese: {作|つく}りたてのパンはおいしい。
{作|つく}りたての{料理|りょうり}を{出|だ}してくれた。
examples.english: They served me a freshly prepared dish.

examples.japanese: この{豆腐|とうふ}は{作|つく}りたてだから、{味|あじ}が{全然|ぜんぜん}{違|ちが}う。
examples.english: This tofu is freshly made, so the taste is completely different.

notes:
Formed from {作|つく}る (to make) + たて (just done). The たて suffix attaches to the stem of verbs to mean "just [verb]ed" and implies the result is still in its freshest or most desirable state.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {作|つく}りたてのパン: freshly baked bread
- {作|つく}りたての{料理|りょうり}: freshly prepared food
- {作|つく}りたての{弁当|べんとう}: a freshly made bento

OTHER WORDS WITH たて:
- {焼|や}きたて: freshly baked/grilled
- {炊|た}きたて: freshly cooked (rice)
- {揚|あ}げたて: freshly deep-fried
- {出来|でき}たて: just completed/ready

USAGE:
Typically used with the particle の to modify a noun: {作|つく}りたての＋noun. Very common in food contexts, where freshness is a selling point. Signs at bakeries and restaurants often advertise {作|つく}りたて items.
